review_type: read-only selected cross-report and internal consistency audit
limitations: No exhaustive source-date or Reuters metadata audit was attempted; parent and november_markets own that work.
The review sampled prose and stance/action consistency; it is not a claim to have checked every factual sentence.
No web or git was used. Specs/tools were not edited.

samples.scope: All 20 weekday specs: US Rates & Curve
samples.result: 20-observation direction/curve descriptors and quoted 2Y/10Y/spread compared with own-date cards; no inconsistency found. Five-observation claims inspected where present, including Nov6 and Nov18; no mismatch found.

samples.scope: All 20 weekday specs: China PMIs & Activity / Credit Impulse
samples.result: Read monthly-period wording. September loan evidence precedes October credit evidence; later October surveys/activity are not mislabeled as November actuals. Nov28 PMI poll remains a forecast. No period contradiction found in this sample.

samples.scope: Nov3/4/6/11/14/18/25/28: geo stances and Playbook paragraphs
samples.result: Selected actions and upgrade/reduction conditions align with respective stance/labels apart from the Nov6 AU certainty issue recorded below. A bearish broad country stance can legitimately coexist with selected longs or onshore-over-offshore relative positions.

Read all four scenarios on each date. Scenario conditions generally remain conditional; no issue was raised merely because a title anticipates a possible outcome or because an economic transmission is conditional.

samples.scope: All 20 weekday specs: split/corporate-action and old-level text search; targeted reads of hits
samples.result: No Netflix/NFLX or Comcast/CMCSA absolute-price references found. Explicit Nov6 SMCI/PLTR and FX old-level comparisons were read; no split-crossing old-price problem found in this sample. Announced ServiceNow split wording has no comparative price level attached.

samples.scope: All 20 weekday specs: source-validation/writing-instruction phrase search; targeted reads of hits
samples.result: Four optional retail voice edits and one optional holiday wording edit recorded below; normal uncertainty/forecast qualifications retained when they help interpretation.

samples.scope: Nov17: US curve, CN PMI/credit, all geo Playbooks, all anticipatory scenarios, phrase-search hits
samples.result: US 3.62%/4.14%, +52bp spread and +21/+15bp bear flattening match card. October/September periods and pending Nvidia/jobs/Walmart/rare-earth scenarios are clear. JP currency-hedge inconsistency was repaired by the writer and rechecked; no further issue in this sample.

findings.quote: Palantir / PLTR — beat, raise, then split the stock
findings.reason: The title reads as an announced/completed stock split, while the supporting Drivers paragraph describes only stock-split chatter and a speculative question.
findings.suggested_change: Retitle to `Palantir / PLTR — beat, raise, then stock-split chatter`.

findings.reason: The label makes the end of easing categorical while its own Macro Stance attributes only `possibly done easing` to Reuters and treats future policy changes conditionally.
findings.suggested_change: Use `on hold / easing constrained` or another forecast-aware label.

instances.quote: The useful social interpretation is the intensity of the leadership narrative, not an invented measure of platform sentiment.
The nearest useful attention evidence is the breadth of financial coverage and the visible share response, rather than an invented count of posts or retail orders.
This is a trade with named public advocates rather than a fabricated measure of message-board enthusiasm.
That is concrete evidence of enthusiasm rather than an invented online mood.

findings.reason: These comparisons describe avoidance of fabricated evidence rather than explaining an investor mechanism. The surrounding cited public-advocacy and mainstream-attention analysis is useful and can stand directly.
findings.suggested_change: State the observed attention and its investment implication directly; remove the invented/fabricated comparisons.

findings.quote: the absence of a Thursday US cash session should not be described as a fresh vote of confidence from those markets
findings.reason: The holiday qualification is useful, but `should not be described` reads as an instruction to a writer.
findings.suggested_change: State the investment implication directly, for example: `Thursday’s holiday leaves those US readings unchanged; the next cash session will test whether the improvement persists.`

findings.quote: hedge yen exposure if a currency reversal starts removing exporters' translation support
findings.reason: A yen appreciation that weakens exporter earnings raises the value of unhedged yen. Adding an FX hedge removes that offset, contrary to the intended exporter risk reduction.
findings.suggested_change: Reduce exporter beta if yen appreciation removes translation support.
findings.resolution: Current spec says `reduce exporter beta if a sharp yen appreciation starts removing translation support`.
